description:
Pipeline run for an LWR. Existing: op-wqk.10 (ipwr_sim_v1), op-wqk.11 (abwr_sim_v1), docs ipwr.md and bwr.md. op-6p2 records that bwr.md contradicts itself on bedok's status — resolve that first.

CHOOSE A PUBLISHED BENCHMARK, not a plant. Candidates: BEAVRS (MIT, PWR, full-core with measured data), or a single pin-cell / assembly from a standard set for a first pass. A pin cell is the right FIRST run for this whole epic — it is the cheapest possible end-to-end exercise of all six stages and will find the pipeline's breaks before an expensive geometry does. Recommend starting here regardless of which reactor is the headline.
TARGETS: pin-cell k-inf against reference, then Doppler and moderator-density coefficients, then an assembly.
ENDF NEEDED: U-235, U-238 (have), O-16, H-1, Zr, B-10 (missing), plus the H-in-H2O TSL, which is the one that matters most for a thermal water system and is NOT in reference-data/endf.
HARDEST STAGE: none, and that is the point — this is the control case where every stage should work, so a failure here is a pipeline defect rather than a physics-modelling gap.

Parent: op-wpi0

description: GH #37 §I. Blender's bundled LoopTools add-on: Bridge; Circle (loop -> best-fit circle); Curve (relax a loop to a smooth curve); Flatten (loop -> best-fit plane); GStretch; Loft (bridge multiple loops); Relax; Space (even spacing along a loop); Subdivide. Several reuse the landed sparse-solve / parameterization machinery.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: loop_tools.rs: circle (best-fit plane + circle, even angular spacing), flatten (project onto best-fit plane), relax (Laplacian along the loop), curve (Catmull-Rom through every keep-th anchor), space (equal arc-length redistribution), gstretch (redistribute along an external stroke polyline), bridge + loft (delegate to bridge::bridge_edge_loops), subdivide (loop-edge midpoint split, cuts bounding faces in two). 8 tests, clippy-clean.

title: outram-blender: LoopTools (bridge, circle, curve, flatten, gstretch, loft, relax, space, subdivide)

description:
A declared-but-unimplemented gap with a known location, so this is a well-bounded first coding task.

CURRENT STATE: the packed-bed pressure-drop variant is declared WITH its citation at crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../fluid_component_calculation/mod.rs:48 and is a todo!() at :161. Meanwhile the gFHR pebble-bed components carry the comment "not putting in ergun equation yet" SEVENTEEN times and use pipe friction on a pebble-derived hydraulic diameter instead — so the wrong correlation is currently in use in more than one place.

SCOPE: implement the Ergun form (viscous plus inertial terms in bed voidage and particle diameter) and the KTA correlation used for pebble beds specifically, then replace the seventeen pipe-friction stand-ins. Verify against the analytical limits and published packed-bed data with the numbers recorded in the test doc comment per the V&V rule.

Note the TUAS porous-media component states its own gap: pressure-drop correlations are not properly implemented so it behaves like a pipe. This bead closes that.
title: HTR-10: Ergun / KTA packed-bed pressure drop — implement the existing todo!()
